does: Toasts a little flour in olive oil, takes the pan off the heat to stir in sweet and hot paprika, then whisks in water and tomato paste and simmers it to a thin, glossy, brick-red sauce with a sharp bite, to spoon over fried potatoes.

intro.what: This salsa brava cooks a flour base, adds paprika away from heat and simmers it into a glossy red sauce.
intro.why: It teaches you to protect paprika from scorching while building a sauce loose enough to flow over potatoes.

how: Warm the olive oil in a small pan over a low heat. Stir in the flour and cook it, stirring, until it smells nutty and has only just darkened.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sweet paprika and the hot paprika. Paprika scorches in hot oil and turns the sauce bitter.
Whisk in the tomato paste, then pour in the water a little at a time, whisking smooth after each addition. Add a crushed clove of garlic if it is liked.
Put the pan back on a low heat and simmer, whisking now and then, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon lightly. Season it with salt at the end.
Keep it warm and spoon it over the potatoes at the last moment, so that they stay crisp.

cues.text: A smooth sauce the colour of brick that coats the back of a spoon in a thin, glossy layer.
Smoky and warm with a bite from the hot paprika, and no raw taste of flour.
Toasty and sweet, with no burnt edge.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring the paprika into hot oil, so that it scorches and the sauce turns bitter.
mistakes.fix: Take the pan off the heat first and stir it in at once.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in all the water at once, which leaves lumps of flour.
mistakes.fix: Pour it in a little at a time, whisking smooth after each addition.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the sauce get too thick, so that it clings to the potatoes as a paste.
mistakes.fix: Loosen it with a little water until it flows off the spoon.

quiz.question: What body should this salsa brava have?
choices: A stiff flour paste that holds a firm mound.
A watery liquid without any spoon coating.
A thin glossy coating that flows from the spoon.
quiz.because: The sauce should lightly coat and flow, rather than cling as a heavy paste.

quiz.question: When do you stir paprika into the flour and oil?
choices: After taking the pan off the heat.
While the oil is at its hottest on the flame.
Before leaving it to fry dark and dry.
quiz.because: Paprika scorches readily in hot oil, so move the pan away from the heat first.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches the finished sauce?
choices: Pale sauce with dry flour lumps.
Smooth brick red with a thin glossy spoon coating.
A dark grainy paste that will not flow.
quiz.because: A smooth light coating shows the gradual liquid addition and gentle simmer have formed the sauce.

quiz.question: The sauce has become a paste that clings heavily. What would you do?
choices: Reduce it further to remove more water.
Add extra flour to thicken it again.
Loosen it with a little water until it flows.
quiz.because: A little water restores the flowing consistency intended for spooning over potatoes.

variant_of.differs: The fat is olive oil and not butter, the flour is only lightly toasted, the paprika goes in off the heat, and the sauce stays thin and sharp. A roux is cooked to a set colour and is the thickener of a smooth white or brown sauce.
